audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Yasuo Levels 2-3 and called Levels 1, 4-5 and 6 Skill, while whys[0] through whys[4] all describe Wukong winning those five rows outright ('Levels 1-2 are yours', 'you win the extended trade cleanly').
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Wukong for rows 0-4 and Yasuo for rows 5-6, and the content prose already says exactly that. No mirror exists yet, so these values set the reference for the yasuo__wukong page.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-4 set to Wukong as matched phases[N].side + win[N] pairs, ratings normalised across all seven rows, and the five stage explanations rewritten to name the mechanic that gives Wukong the row.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why was the generic 'Cyclone's double knockup wins every committed brawl' line, and phases[5]/phases[6] named no timing beyond 'Black Cleaver' and a carry-threat number.
audit.why: Last Breath is 70/50/30s and Riot's text says it blinks to an Airborne enemy champion — with no knock-up on you it does not fire at all, which is the real Level 6 story. Yasuo's spike is his first crit item, where Way of the Wanderer's movement shield plus crit chance win short trades, and at two items Wind Wall is a 4-second block every 17s at max rank.
audit.corrected: Level 6 stage now states the Airborne requirement and the 70s cooldown; the first-item and 2+ item stages now name the crit-item and shield spike and the Wind Wall uptime.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] 'E-Q burst him', dontsFull[1] 'Fight his level-6 resets' and dontsFull[2] 'Eat his R follow-up' carried bodies copied from other rows. Steel Tempest's 4s cooldown and two-stack knock-up rule, Sweeping Blade's same-target lockout, and the fact that any ally's displacement also enables Last Breath were all absent.
audit.why: Riot's text: Steel Tempest grants a stack on hit and only fires the knocking-up whirlwind at 2 stacks, on a flat 4s. Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds, which is why a second body in the trade strands him. Last Breath blinks to any Airborne enemy champion, so a jungler's knock-up arms it just as well as his own.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns carry the Airborne requirement, the 70s, the 4s Steel Tempest and Wind Wall's 4s/25s; dosFull[2].d states punishing between Q casts; dontsFull[1].d states that the ult resets Gathering Storm stacks and not its own cooldown; dontsFull[2].d states the ally-CC trigger.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] says Yasuo can 'Hold Windwall to eat your E dash and Cyclone follow-up', and late/spikes[3] say Wind Wall neutralises your all-in.
audit.why: Riot's description is only 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds'. The kit's derived 'terrain: blocks paths and dashes' flag contradicts that description, and dash/knock-up eligibility against Wind Wall is exactly the class of mechanic the kit files mark as unknown. I could not verify it either way and Wukong's own kit was absent from the brief.

edits.before: Q-AA poke wins the short exchanges. Identify how Yasuo contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Steel Tempest needs two stacks to knock you up and at Level 1 he has nothing else — walk at him and take the trade.

edits.before: W clone bails out any misstep and baits his answer. Only take the trade when Yasuo's Last Breath is down.
edits.after: Still no Wind Wall for him at 2, so Crushing Blow and your autos land clean while his Q is only a 4s poke.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Yasuo must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online: Sweeping Blade cannot re-target the same enemy for a few seconds, so the clone strands him mid-trade.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Last Breath's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your stretch before crit items: his shield only builds while he is moving, so open the trade the moment he stops to last-hit.

edits.before: Cyclone’s double knockup wins every committed brawl. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Yasuo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Last Breath only fires at an Airborne target, so if he never lands the two-stack knock-up his 70s ultimate stays in his pocket.

edits.before: Black Cleaver is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Last Breath's cooldown.
edits.after: His first crit item flips it — the movement shield plus crits win every short trade.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Yasuo carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on he out-duels you: crits, the movement shield, and 4 seconds of Wind Wall every 17s at max rank. Group instead.

edits.before: - Yasuo Last Breath: matchup-defining — His all-in after knockup. Fight when down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Last Breath: 70s at rank 1 and it needs an Airborne target — deny the knock-up and it is dead weight. - Steel Tempest: 4s, and it only knocks up on the second stack. - Wind Wall: 4s of cover on 25s at rank 1.

edits.before: His all-in after knockup. Fight when down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It needs an Airborne target — deny the knock-up and the 70s ult never fires.

edits.after: Steel Tempest is only 4s — punish between casts, not after.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.

edits.before: Burning W before the trade starts — the clone IS your defense, and committing without it means eating his full combo.
